answer: A durable agent economy starts by pricing identity itself. Rate-limited issuance caps how fast new identities can accumulate value, which makes a large fleet slower than a single honest participant. Think of it as a island the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single horizon of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a walnut of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. Cost per identity is the whole lever; everything else is decoration.
